description: Adapted from Abelson, Sussman & Sussman, Structure and Interpretation of Computer Programs, 2nd ed. Louis squares the items of [1 2 3 4] iteratively, putting each new square in front of the result built so far, so his list comes out reversed. Compute Louis's result, then the correctly ordered list of squares, where each new square goes at the end. Print both vectors, Louis's first, each with disp(mat2str(...)).

description: Adapted from Abelson, Sussman & Sussman, Structure and Interpretation of Computer Programs, 2nd ed. Take the four sequences (1 2 3), (4 5 6), (7 8 9) and (10 11 12) as the rows of a matrix. Combine all the first elements, all the second elements and all the third elements with an accumulation: first with addition, then with multiplication. Print the vector of sums and then the vector of products, each with disp(mat2str(...)).

license: CC BY-SA 4.0 — Abelson, Sussman, Sussman, «Structure and Interpretation of Computer Programs», 2nd ed. (mitpress.mit.edu); adapted, under the same license
description: Adapted from Abelson, Sussman & Sussman, Structure and Interpretation of Computer Programs, 2nd ed. Sets are stored as unordered vectors without duplicates. Compute the union of set1 = [1 3 5 7] and set2 = [3 4 5]. The result is set2 followed by the elements of set1 that are not members of set2, kept in their original order. Print it with disp(mat2str(u)).

description: Adapted from Abelson, Sussman & Sussman, Structure and Interpretation of Computer Programs, 2nd ed. Build a Huffman tree over the symbol weights [8 3 1 1 1 1 1 1] (A through H) by repeatedly merging the two smallest weights into one node until a single node is left. Along the way, add up the weights of all merged nodes; this total is the number of bits needed to encode a message with these frequencies. Print the total and then the weight of the root node, each with printf('%d\n', ...).
A rectangle has width w = 7 and height h = 12. Compute its area and its perimeter. Print the area first with printf('%d\n', area), then the perimeter with printf('%d\n', perimeter).
Compute the area of a circle with radius r = 3 using the constant pi. Print the area with printf('%.4f\n', area).
Build the vector of the squares of the integers 1 to 6 using an elementwise power. Print each element on its own line with the format '%d\n'.
Given the vector v = [3 1 4 1 5 9 2 6], count how many elements are strictly greater than 3. Print the count with printf('%d\n', count).
Compute the average of the numbers v = [4 8 15 16 23 42]. Print the average with printf('%.2f\n', avg).
Compute three remainders: mod(17, 5), rem(-17, 5) and mod(-17, 5). Print each result on its own line in that order with the format '%d\n'.
Apply four rounding functions: floor to 7.8, ceil to 7.2, round to -2.5 and fix to -2.7. Print the four results in that order, each on its own line, with the format '%d\n'.
Build the range that starts at 10 and counts down in steps of 3 without going below 0 (10:-3:0). Print the vector with disp(mat2str(v)).
solution:
v = 10:-3:0;
disp(mat2str(v));

description: Compute the product of the integers from 1 to 6. Print the product with printf('%d\n', p).
solution:
p = prod(1:6);
printf('%d\n', p);

description: From the integers 1 to 20, select the even numbers and add them up. Print the sum with printf('%d\n', s).
A student scored 42 points out of a possible 56. Compute the score as a percentage. Print it with printf('%.1f%%\n', pct).

A shopping list has unit prices prices = [2.5 4 1.25] and quantities qty = [4 3 8]. Compute the total cost, i.e. the sum of each price times its quantity. Print the total with printf('%.2f\n', total).
Given the vector v = [12 7 19 3 25 14 8], count how many elements lie between 8 and 20 inclusive. Print the count with printf('%d\n', count).
Given the vector v = [9 4 7 2 8 2 5], find its smallest value and the position of the first place where it occurs. Print both on one line with printf('%d %d\n', m, idx).
Given the vector v = [1 4 9 16 25], compute the differences between consecutive elements. Print the result with disp(mat2str(d)).
A right triangle has legs a = 5 and b = 12. Compute the length of the hypotenuse with the Pythagorean formula. Print it with printf('%d\n', c).
Given the vector v = [3 -1 4 -1 5 -9 2], replace every negative element with 0 and keep the other elements unchanged. Print the resulting vector with disp(mat2str(v)).
Compute the sum of 1/k^2 for k = 1, 2, 3, 4 using elementwise operations on the range 1:4. Print the sum with printf('%.4f\n', s).
Convert the Celsius temperatures c = [0 25 100 -40] to Fahrenheit using F = C*9/5 + 32. Print each Fahrenheit value on its own line with the format '%d\n'.
Given the exam scores v = [45 67 89 32 50 76 49 90], a score passes if it is at least 50. Compute the percentage of passing scores. Print it with printf('%.1f\n', pct).
Given the vector v = [4 -2 7 0 -5 9 -1], count how many elements are negative and add up the elements that are strictly positive. Print both on one line with printf('%d %d\n', count, total).
Sort the vector v = [15 3 42 8 23 4] in descending order. Print the sorted row vector with disp(mat2str(s)).

Given the vector v = [5 3 5 1 3 9 1 5], find its distinct values in ascending order. Print how many distinct values there are with printf('%d\n', n), then print the distinct values with disp(mat2str(u)).

Given the vector v = [2 7 1 8 2 8 1 8], find the index of the first element greater than 5, then find all the indices where v equals 8. Print the first index with printf('%d\n', ...), then print each index of 8 on its own line with printf('%d\n', ...).

For the matrix A = [1 2 3; 4 5 6; 7 8 9], compute the sum of each row and the sum of each column. Print the three row sums (top to bottom), then the three column sums (left to right), one per line, with printf('%d\n', ...).
Compute the matrix product C of A = [1 2; 3 4] and B = [5 6; 7 8], i.e. C = A*B (a true matrix product, not elementwise). Print C with disp(mat2str(C)).
Transpose the matrix M = [1 2 3; 4 5 6] to get B. Print the number of rows and columns of B with printf('%d %d\n', size(B)), then print B with disp(mat2str(B)).
For the matrix A = [2 0 1; 3 5 4; 6 1 7], take its main diagonal as a row vector and print it with disp(mat2str(d)). Then print the sum of the diagonal (the trace) with printf('%d\n', t).

The matrix scores = [80 90 70; 60 75 90; 100 85 80] has one row per student and one column per exam. Compute the mean of each column, i.e. the average score of each exam. Print the three means, one per line, with printf('%.2f\n', ...).

Given the vector v = [12 45 7 33 28 50 19 3], select the elements between 10 and 30 inclusive and keep them in their original order. Print how many there are with printf('%d\n', n), then print each selected element on its own line with printf('%d\n', ...).
Five players have ids = [101 102 103 104 105] and the matching scores = [88 72 95 60 81]. Print the player ids ordered from highest to lowest score, one per line, with printf('%d\n', ...).

Given the vector v = [4 9 2 7 9 3], look up each of the targets 7, 5 and 9 in that order. For each target, find the index of its first occurrence in v, or use 0 if it does not occur. Print each result on its own line with printf('%d\n', k).

For the matrix A = [3 -1 4; -1 5 -9; 2 -6 5], count its negative entries and print the count with printf('%d\n', n). Then replace every negative entry with 0 and print the resulting matrix with disp(mat2str(A)).
Given the string s = 'Hello World 2026', pick out its uppercase letters in order and print them with disp(...). Then count the digit characters in s and print the count with printf('%d\n', n).

For the matrix A = [4 9 2; 3 5 7; 8 1 6], find the largest value in each column and the row index where it occurs. Print the row vector of column maxima with disp(mat2str(m)), then the row vector of their row indices with disp(mat2str(r)).

For the matrix A = [1 0 3; 0 5 0; 7 0 9], find the row and column of every entry greater than 4, in column-major order (go down column 1 first, then column 2, and so on). Print each position on its own line as the row, a space and the column, using the format '%d %d\n'.

Build the table T = table([1;2;3;4], [85;92;78;90], 'VariableNames', {'id','score'}). Print the mean of the score column with printf('%.2f\n', ...), then print how many scores are at least 85 with printf('%d\n', ...).

Build the table T = table([101;102;103;104;105], [30;12;45;20;41], 'VariableNames', {'id','price'}) and sort its rows by price in descending order with sortrows. Print each row of the sorted table on its own line as the id, a space and the price, using the format '%d %d\n'.

Build the table T = table([1;2;1;3;2;1], [10;20;30;40;50;60], 'VariableNames', {'dept','sales'}). Use groupsummary to find, for each dept, the number of rows and the total sales. Print one line per dept in ascending dept order as the dept, the row count and the total sales, using the format '%d %d %d\n'.

Build the table T = table([2;7;4;9;6], [10;3;8;5;4], 'VariableNames', {'qty','price'}). Select the rows where qty is greater than 5. Print how many rows were selected with printf('%d\n', n), then print the total value of those rows (the sum of qty times price) with printf('%d\n', total).
Use a for loop with an accumulator to compute the sum of the squares of the integers 1 through 10 (1^2 + 2^2 + ... + 10^2). Print the sum with printf('%d\n', s).

For each value in the vector [-3 0 7], decide whether it is negative, zero or positive. Print one line per value, in order, with printf('%d negative
', x), printf('%d zero
', x) or printf('%d positive
', x).

Write a local function collatz_steps(n) that counts the Collatz steps needed to reach 1. In each step, n becomes n/2 if n is even and 3*n+1 if n is odd. Call it on 6, 7 and 27 in that order, and print each count with printf('%d\n', c).
Write a recursive local function myfact(n) that returns n! (with 0! = 1). Call it on 0, 5 and 10 in that order, and print each result with printf('%d\n', r).

Write a recursive local function fib(n) that returns the n-th Fibonacci number, where fib(1) = 1, fib(2) = 1 and fib(n) = fib(n-1) + fib(n-2). Call it on 10, 15 and 20 in that order, and print each result with printf('%d\n', r).

Write a recursive local function egcd(a, b) that computes the greatest common divisor with Euclid's algorithm: gcd(a, 0) = a, otherwise gcd(a, b) = gcd(b, mod(a, b)). Do not use the builtin gcd. Call it on the pairs (48, 18), (1071, 462) and (17, 5) in that order, and print each result with printf('%d\n', g).

Write a recursive local function mypow(b, n) that computes b^n for a non-negative integer n by exponentiation by squaring: b^0 = 1; for even n, compute h = b^(n/2) recursively and return h*h; for odd n, return b * b^(n-1). Call it on (2, 10), (3, 5) and (5, 0) in that order, and print each result with printf('%d\n', r).

Write a recursive local function digsum(n) that returns the sum of the decimal digits of a non-negative integer n. Call it on 12345, 9875 and 7 in that order, and print each result with printf('%d\n', s).

Find all perfect numbers from 2 to 500. A perfect number equals the sum of its proper divisors (all positive divisors smaller than the number itself), e.g. 6 = 1 + 2 + 3. Print each perfect number in increasing order on its own line with printf('%d\n', n).

Collect all primes below 30 into a row vector p by trial division: a number n from 2 to 29 is prime if no d from 2 to floor(sqrt(n)) divides it (stop testing at the first divisor found). Print the vector with disp(mat2str(p)).
Add the integers 1, 2, 3, ... to a running sum and stop as soon as the sum is greater than 1000. Print the last integer added and the sum at that point with printf('%d %d\n', n, s).

Write a local function popcount(n) that counts the 1 bits in the binary representation of a non-negative integer n with a while loop, using mod and floor division by 2. Call it on 1000, 255 and 1024 in that order, and print each count with printf('%d\n', c).

Give each score in the vector [95 83 71 65 42] a letter grade: 'A' for 90 and above, 'B' for 80 and above, 'C' for 70 and above, 'D' for 60 and above, otherwise 'F'. For each score, in order, print the score and its grade with printf('%d %s\n', s, g).

Write a local function isleap(y) that returns true if the year y is a Gregorian leap year: it is divisible by 4 and not by 100, or it is divisible by 400. Call it on the years 1900, 2000, 2024 and 2023 in that order. For each year, print the year and the result (1 or 0) with printf('%d %d\n', y, isleap(y)).

Write a local function revdigits(n) that reverses the decimal digits of a positive integer n with a while loop. Leading zeros of the result disappear, so 1200 becomes 21. Call it on 12345, 1200 and 7 in that order, and print each result with printf('%d\n', r).

Play FizzBuzz for the integers 1 to 15. For each integer, print 'FizzBuzz' if it is divisible by 15, 'Fizz' if it is divisible by 3, 'Buzz' if it is divisible by 5, and otherwise the number itself. Print one item per line: the words with disp and the numbers with printf('%d\n', k).

Write a local function tritype(a, b, c) that classifies three side lengths. It returns 'invalid' if some pair of sides has a sum less than or equal to the third side. Otherwise it returns 'equilateral' if all three sides are equal, 'isosceles' if exactly two are equal, and 'scalene' if all differ. Call it on (3,3,3), (3,4,5), (5,5,8) and (1,2,3) in that order, and print each result with disp.
Loop over the characters of the string 'programming language' and count the lowercase vowels (a, e, i, o, u). Print the count with printf('%d\n', c).

Write a recursive local function tobin(n) that returns the binary representation of a positive integer n as a char string: for n < 2 the result is the single digit, otherwise it is tobin(floor(n/2)) followed by the digit mod(n,2). Call it on 10, 37 and 1 in that order, and print each string with disp.
Use nested for loops to count the pairs of integers (i, j) with 1 <= i < j <= 20 where i + j is divisible by 5. Print the count with printf('%d\n', c).

Write a recursive local function hanoi(n) that returns the minimum number of moves needed to solve the Tower of Hanoi with n disks: 0 moves for 0 disks, otherwise twice the moves for n-1 disks plus 1. Call it on 3, 5 and 10 in that order, and print each result with printf('%d\n', m).
Given the string s = 'hello world', reverse the order of its characters. Print the reversed string with printf('%s\n', r).
Given the string s = 'Programming Language', count its vowels (a, e, i, o, u), ignoring case. Print the count with printf('%d\n', n).
Given the string s = 'mississippi', count how many times each of the characters 'i', 's' and 'p' appears, in that order. For each one print a line with printf('%c: %d\n', c, count).
Given the string s = 'the cat sat on the mat', replace every occurrence of the substring 'at' with 'og'. Print the result with printf('%s\n', t).
expected: the cog sog on the mog

description: Given the string s = '   data science  ', remove the leading and trailing spaces. Print the trimmed string in square brackets followed by its length with printf('[%s] %d\n', t, length(t)).
Given the string s = 'banana', find the starting positions of every occurrence of the substring 'ana', counting overlapping occurrences. Print each position on its own line with the format '%d\n'.

Write a function ispal(s) that returns true if the string s is a palindrome after converting it to lower case and removing all spaces. Apply it to 'A man a plan a canal Panama', 'Never odd or even' and 'Step on no cats', in that order. Print each result (1 or 0) on its own line with printf('%d\n', r).

Build the text 'Item-01,Item-02,Item-03' for the numbers 1 to 3: each label is 'Item-' followed by the number padded to two digits with a leading zero, and the labels are joined by commas with no trailing comma. Print the text with printf('%s\n', s).
Given the number n = 90817, get its decimal digits as a vector. Print the sum of the digits with printf('%d\n', total), then print the number of digits with printf('%d\n', count).
The string s = '12,7,30,5' holds comma-separated integers. Parse them into a numeric vector. Print their sum with printf('%d\n', total), then print their maximum with printf('%d\n', m).
The string s = 'Total: 42.50 EUR' holds an amount between the colon and the currency word. Extract the amount as a number and double it. Print the doubled amount with printf('%.2f\n', y).
Given the name s = 'grace brewster murray hopper' (words separated by single spaces), build the initials: the first letter of each word, in upper case. Print them with printf('%s\n', ini).
Given the vector v = [3 14 15 92], format it as text: the numbers separated by a comma and a space, inside square brackets. Print the text with printf('%s\n', t), so the output is [3, 14, 15, 92].
Given the string s = 'the quick brown fox' (words separated by single spaces), capitalize the first letter of each word and leave the rest unchanged. Print the result with printf('%s\n', t).

Given the string s = '  one two   three four  ', count its words. A word is a maximal run of non-space characters, and the words may be separated by several spaces, with extra spaces at the start and end. Print the count with printf('%d\n', n).

Given the string s = 'aaabccddddea', collapse every run of repeated consecutive characters into a single character. Characters that appear again later, after a different character, are kept. Print the result with printf('%s\n', t).

Run-length encode the string s = 'aaabccdddd': replace each run of equal consecutive characters with the character followed by the length of the run, so 'aaa' becomes 'a3'. Print the encoded string with printf('%s\n', out).

Given the string s = 'Hello World 42', swap the case of every letter (lowercase becomes uppercase and uppercase becomes lowercase) and leave all other characters unchanged. Print the result with printf('%s\n', t).

Given the 10-digit phone number string s = '5551234567', format it as '(AAA) BBB-CCCC', where AAA is the first three digits, BBB the next three and CCCC the last four. Print the formatted number with printf('%s\n', t).

The following loop program computes the sum of squares of a vector: `v = [3 1 4 1 5 9 2 6]; s = 0; for k = 1:numel(v); s = s + v(k)^2; end; printf('%d\n', s);`. Write an equivalent vectorized mlab program without any loop, using the same vector v = [3 1 4 1 5 9 2 6]. It must print exactly the same output, which is the sum printed with printf('%d\n', s).

The following loop program counts the even elements of a vector: `v = [7 2 8 3 5 1 9 4]; c = 0; for k = 1:numel(v); if mod(v(k), 2) == 0; c = c + 1; end; end; printf('%d\n', c);`. Write an equivalent vectorized mlab program without loops or if statements, using the same vector v = [7 2 8 3 5 1 9 4]. It must print exactly the same output: the count printed with printf('%d\n', c).

The following loop program prints the running totals of a vector: `v = [2 5 1 7 3]; s = 0; for k = 1:numel(v); s = s + v(k); printf('%d\n', s); end`. Write an equivalent vectorized mlab program without any loop, using the same vector v = [2 5 1 7 3]. It must print exactly the same output: each running total on its own line with the format '%d\n'.
solution:
v = [2 5 1 7 3];
printf('%d\n', cumsum(v));

description: The following loop program prints the differences between consecutive elements of a vector: `v = [4 9 7 12 20]; for k = 2:numel(v); printf('%d\n', v(k) - v(k-1)); end`. Write an equivalent vectorized mlab program without any loop, using the same vector v = [4 9 7 12 20]. It must print exactly the same output: each difference on its own line with the format '%d\n'.
solution:
v = [4 9 7 12 20];
printf('%d\n', diff(v));

description: The following loop program finds the largest element of a vector and the position where it first occurs: `v = [4 11 7 11 3]; m = v(1); p = 1; for k = 2:numel(v); if v(k) > m; m = v(k); p = k; end; end; printf('%d %d\n', m, p);`. Write an equivalent mlab program without any loop, using the same vector v = [4 11 7 11 3]. It must print exactly the same output: the maximum and its first index on one line with printf('%d %d\n', m, p).

The following loop program fills a vector element by element: `y = zeros(1, 6); for k = 1:6; y(k) = k^2 - k; end; disp(mat2str(y));`. Write an equivalent vectorized mlab program without any loop that builds the same vector for k = 1 to 6 and prints exactly the same output with disp(mat2str(y)).

The following loop program replaces the negative elements of a vector with zero: `v = [3 -1 4 -1 -5 9]; for k = 1:numel(v); if v(k) < 0; v(k) = 0; end; end; disp(mat2str(v));`. Write an equivalent vectorized mlab program without loops or if statements (use logical indexing), using the same vector v = [3 -1 4 -1 -5 9]. It must print exactly the same output with disp(mat2str(v)).

The following loop program collects the positions where a vector equals 5: `v = [5 2 5 8 5 1]; idx = []; for k = 1:numel(v); if v(k) == 5; idx(end+1) = k; end; end; printf('%d\n', idx);`. Write an equivalent vectorized mlab program without any loop, using the same vector v = [5 2 5 8 5 1]. It must print exactly the same output: each index on its own line with the format '%d\n'.

The following nested-loop program prints the row sums of a matrix: `A = [1 2 3; 4 5 6; 7 8 10]; for i = 1:3; s = 0; for j = 1:3; s = s + A(i,j); end; printf('%d\n', s); end`. Write an equivalent vectorized mlab program without any loop, using the same matrix A = [1 2 3; 4 5 6; 7 8 10]. It must print exactly the same output: each row sum on its own line with the format '%d\n'.

The following loop program multiplies the first six odd numbers: `p = 1; for k = 1:6; p = p * (2*k - 1); end; printf('%d\n', p);`. Write an equivalent vectorized mlab program without any loop that computes the same product and prints exactly the same output with printf('%d\n', p).
solution:
p = prod(1:2:11);
printf('%d\n', p);

description: The following loop program computes the mean of the even elements of a vector: `v = [3 8 6 12 7 4]; s = 0; c = 0; for k = 1:numel(v); if mod(v(k), 2) == 0; s = s + v(k); c = c + 1; end; end; printf('%.2f\n', s / c);`. Write an equivalent vectorized mlab program without loops or if statements, using the same vector v = [3 8 6 12 7 4]. It must print exactly the same output: the mean printed with printf('%.2f\n', ...).

The following loop program counts the lowercase vowels in a string: `s = 'hello world'; c = 0; for k = 1:numel(s); if any(s(k) == 'aeiou'); c = c + 1; end; end; printf('%d\n', c);`. Write an equivalent vectorized mlab program without loops or if statements (for example, compare all characters against 'aeiou' at once using implicit expansion), using the same string s = 'hello world'. It must print exactly the same output: the count printed with printf('%d\n', c).

Rewrite this C fragment in mlab so that it prints exactly the same output: `int s = 0; for (int i = 1; i <= 10; i++) if (i % 3 == 0) s += i; printf("%d\n", s);`. The fragment adds up the numbers from 1 to 10 that are divisible by 3. Print the sum with printf('%d\n', s).

Rewrite this C fragment in mlab so that it prints exactly the same output: `int a = 48, b = 18; while (b != 0) { int t = a % b; a = b; b = t; } printf("%d\n", a);`. This is Euclid's algorithm on a = 48 and b = 18. Keep the while loop and use mod for the C % operator. Print the result with printf('%d\n', a).

Rewrite this C fragment in mlab so that it prints exactly the same output: `int n = 7, steps = 0; while (n != 1) { if (n % 2 == 0) n = n / 2; else n = 3 * n + 1; steps++; } printf("%d\n", steps);`. It counts the Collatz steps needed to go from n = 7 down to 1. Print the step count with printf('%d\n', steps).

Rewrite this C fragment in mlab so that it prints exactly the same output: `for (int i = 1; i <= 4; i++) { for (int j = 1; j <= i; j++) printf("*"); printf("\n"); }`. It prints a left-aligned triangle of asterisks with 4 rows, where row i has i asterisks. Print each row with the format '%s\n'.

Sort the vector v = [29 10 14 37 13] in ascending order with insertion sort, without using the sort builtin. Count how many times an element is shifted one position to the right. First print the sorted vector with disp(mat2str(v)), then print the number of shifts with printf('%d\n', shifts).
For the vector v = [3 1 4 1 5 9 2 6], compute the running maximum with a loop: a vector r of the same size where r(k) is the largest of v(1) through v(k). Print r with disp(mat2str(r)).

Given the vector v = [8 3 11 5 7 2] and the target 13, use nested loops to find every pair of indices i < j with v(i) + v(j) == 13. Print each pair on its own line with printf('%d %d\n', i, j), ordered by i and then by j.

Compute the matrix-vector product y = A*x for A = [2 -1 0; 1 3 2; 1 4 -2] and x = [3; 1; 2] with explicit nested loops, without using the * operator on the whole matrix. Print each element of y on its own line with the format '%d\n'.
